subject: Effect estimates dependent on prediction points

messages.author: f09a4f9db82a4609
messages.subject: Effect estimates dependent on prediction points
parts:
Hi,

I am testing some models with non-stationary spatial random effects to predict an outcome variable on a dense grid of prediction points. This to generate a raster map of model predictions. I need a dense grid as some fixed effects vary considerably over short distances, but due to computational limitations estimating the whole prediction grid at once is not possible.

I tried to get around this by splitting the prediction grid into several parts, and doing prediction while fitting to all points with known values (training set)for the outcome variable for each grid part separately. Afterwards I combined them again, thinking that using the same training set would produce the same model every time regardless of the prediction points added. However, I noticed that the fixed parameter mean estimates differ slightly but noticeably in the models linked to each grid part depending on which prediction points I add. Between different sets some fixed parameter estimates vary to up to 1.7%. While this was in itself not too worrying, I decided to compare the estimates of one of the prediction sets to estimates gotten when just fitting the model to the training set without any prediction points, and in that case some mean estimates for fixed effects varied by over 10%.

Is this behavior to be expected, and thus my approach of predicting different parts of the grid in series fundamentally flawed? Or should I look for a mistake in my model setup.

Thanks for your insights and best regards,

Sam

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Effect estimates dependent on prediction points
parts:
Hi,

with so few data there will be a confounding with the intercept and the
spde, and with two of those and a scaling, yes, this can happen. You
have to tighten the model up, either more strict prior for the scaling
or some kind of constr of the spde

you can consider to add constr=T

spde=inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,prior.range = c(2,.1),prior.sigma =
c(1,.5), constr=TRUE)

then scaling is essentially, a different precision for the second
replicate. I don't know if this make sense or not for you.

otherwise, I would suggest to use

control.inla = list(strategy = "adaptive"),
num.threads = "2:1")

and the num.threads argument have now changed in the recent versions.

... also upgrade to R-4.0 and the newest testing version, which will
also be much faster ;-)

All the best
H

and having a model without y[10], is a numerical thing only.

It seems like the tolerance should be tighten in your case. Do you run
with R-4.0 and the newest testing version? It has improvement for the
hyperpar optimisation, and more strict tolerances, that I think should
help in your case.
